root_causes.root_cause: The corpus-ingest-score.js workflow pipeline's Stage 2 guard condition (line 183) short-circuits ALL documents to verdict=ERROR because Stage 1 (Haiku agent) returns a plain string (no schema parameter), and the guard `typeof ingestResult === 'string' && ingestResult.includes('error')` matches the substring 'error' in successful responses. Stage 1's prompt explicitly asks 'Report: ... Any errors', so even a success response (e.g. 'Any errors: none' or 'error: null') contains the substring 'error'. This causes every document to skip Stage 2 (Sonnet fetch of MinIO meta) and Stage 3 (Opus judge) entirely, returning the hardcoded ERROR default with null node_count/chars. The actual ingestion succeeds (converter subprocess writes meta.json to MinIO), but the scoring pipeline never reads those results.
root_causes.code_path: .claude/workflows/corpus-ingest-score.js:183 -> Stage 2 guard condition -> false-positive substring match on Haiku string output
root_causes.suggested_fix: Add a `schema` parameter to Stage 1's agent() call (line 159-179) so it returns structured JSON instead of a free-text string. The prompt already asks for JSON output (`Return a JSON object: { "doc_id": ..., "status": ... }`), but without the `schema` parameter the agent returns unstructured text. Alternatively, change the guard to parse the string as JSON first, or change the substring check to look for `"status":"error"` rather than the bare word 'error'.

root_causes.root_cause: world-stats-pocketbook-2023.pdf (6.1MB) left mid-flight with no MinIO artifact. The converter subprocess has CHILD_TIMEOUT=1770s (29.5 min) and JOB_TIMEOUT=1800s (30 min) in worker.py:48-56. However, preprocess_client.py (used by the pipeline) calls _run_converter_subprocess directly with this same timeout. For a 6.1MB PDF running through Docling conversion, the processing time may exceed this budget, especially on a memory-constrained node where memory_admission gating adds waiting time. Additionally, even if the converter starts, an OOM kill (returncode -9) or timeout would leave no MinIO artifact since the converter writes to MinIO only at completion (converters_cli.py). This is a distinct issue from RC-1: this document genuinely failed to complete processing, while all other 23 documents completed ingestion successfully but had their scores discarded by the pipeline guard bug.
root_causes.code_path: src/pageindex_mcp/worker.py:48-56 (CHILD_TIMEOUT/JOB_TIMEOUT) -> _run_converter_subprocess:245 (asyncio.timeout) -> preprocess_client.py:149 (_run_converter_subprocess call)
root_causes.suggested_fix: Increase JOB_TIMEOUT for large files (e.g., scale timeout proportionally to file size, or introduce a LARGE_FILE_TIMEOUT override). Also add partial-artifact persistence so that even if the converter times out, any completed pages/sections are saved rather than losing all work. As a quick fix, re-run world-stats-pocketbook-2023.pdf in isolation with a higher CHILD_TIMEOUT or on a machine with more resources.

root_causes.root_cause: The image_enrichment_promoted branch in classify_verdict (helpers.py lines 1198-1203) returns PASS when content_class is flat_prose/flat_mixed and image_enrichment_ratio >= 0.8, but performs NO check on node_count, char volume, or tree depth. Any flat doc with a high image-enrichment ratio gets PASS regardless of actual content extracted -- 2 blocks/38 chars or 2 blocks/123 chars both pass. This contravenes Hard Rule 5 (never silently persist a low-quality tree). The branch was introduced in RFC-021 (QF2a) and hoisted above the max_leaf_ratio hard-FAIL in RFC-022 (B2-B), but a minimum content-volume floor was never added at either stage.
root_causes.code_path: src/pageindex_mcp/helpers.py :: classify_verdict() lines 1198-1203
root_causes.suggested_fix: Add a minimum content-volume guard to the image_enrichment_promoted branch: require node_count >= 1 AND total char count >= some floor (e.g., 200 chars) before returning PASS. Documents below the floor should fall through to MARGINAL with a descriptive reason like 'image_enrichment_insufficient_content'. This preserves the legitimate promotion for image-heavy docs (pie charts, scanned tables) while blocking near-empty docs from getting PASS.

root_causes.root_cause: classify_verdict has no hard FAIL return for node_count=0 or zero-char documents. The only FAIL paths are: garbling, reordered, and max_leaf_ratio > 0.75. A document with 0 nodes and 0 chars falls through all PASS gates (which require node_count >= 3) and all promotion paths (which require node_count >= 1 or >= 3), then reaches the final MARGINAL return at line 1296-1302 with reason 'node_count=0'. This means totally empty extraction results get MARGINAL instead of FAIL, masking complete content loss. Previously (Run 8), these docs hit LowQualityTreeError and were stored as ERROR or FAIL; in Run 9, the expanded recovery paths (RFC-025 D3 broadening garbling/node_garbling triggers) route them through flat-path processing, which produces an empty structure that classify_verdict rates as MARGINAL.
root_causes.code_path: src/pageindex_mcp/helpers.py :: classify_verdict() lines 1293-1302 (final MARGINAL return with no preceding FAIL floor for node_count=0)
root_causes.suggested_fix: Add a hard FAIL floor early in classify_verdict: if node_count == 0 or total char volume < some absolute minimum (e.g., 50 chars), return FAIL with reason 'empty_content' or 'below_minimum_content'. This should fire after the garbling/reordered checks but before the PASS gate, ensuring zero-content docs never surface as MARGINAL.

root_causes.root_cause: RFC-025 D0 hysteresis depends on find_prior_verdict() scanning processed/*.meta.json sidecars in MinIO to locate a prior PASS verdict. However, the corpus reingestion pipeline (corpus-ingest / corpus-ingest-score) wipes all derived stores (including processed/*) before starting. When GHV-TKV-Tarif.pdf is re-ingested, no prior sidecar exists -- find_prior_verdict returns None, no hysteresis band is applied, and the base PASS_MAX_LEAF_RATIO=0.30 threshold is used. The doc's max_leaf_ratio of 0.3853 exceeds 0.30, so it gets MARGINAL with reason 'leaf_concentration=0.39'. With hysteresis, _effective_max_leaf would be 0.40 (0.30 + 0.10 band), and 0.3853 < 0.40 would PASS. The feature is structurally dead in the reingestion scenario it was designed for.
root_causes.code_path: src/pageindex_mcp/storage.py :: find_prior_verdict() lines 626-670 (scans processed/*.meta.json that are wiped before reingestion)
root_causes.suggested_fix: Either (a) persist a lightweight verdict-history ledger (e.g., a JSON file in a non-wiped MinIO prefix like 'verdict-history/') that survives the derived-store wipe, and have find_prior_verdict consult it; or (b) separate the wipe into two stages -- wipe processed/*.json and processed/*.meta.json trees but preserve processed/*.meta.json sidecars (or a snapshot of them) until after scoring completes; or (c) export prior verdicts to a Redis hash before the wipe and read from there in find_prior_verdict.

root_causes.root_cause: Docling force-full-page-OCR on scanned/image-dominant Arabic PDFs still produces only `<!-- image -->` markers (PictureItems) rather than extracting text into prose. The image-dominant OCR escalation (RFC-023 D11) fires correctly but the re-conversion with `force_full_page_ocr=True` yields the same image-only markdown. Per-picture Tesseract OCR via `_recover_picture_results` also fails to produce meaningful text for full-page Arabic scans (all results become `decorative=True` or have OCR text below `_PICTURE_OCR_MIN_CHARS=20`). `splice_figure_markers` then strips all decorative markers (STRIP_SKIPPED_IMAGE_MARKERS defaults to true), leaving empty flat markdown. `route_and_extract_flat('')` produces 0 blocks / 0 chars. This is the KNOWN image-OCR-never-fires defect documented in memory `ocr-image-block-conflation-2026-07-27`. RFC-017 D0 (page-coverage filter) and D1 (standalone image enrichment) are both implemented but do not address the core scanned-PDF-to-empty pipeline gap. RFC-023 D11 (image-dominant OCR escalation) is implemented but the escalation itself produces no content for these documents.
root_causes.code_path: src/pageindex_mcp/converters.py::_recover_picture_results (line 1939) -> _recover_picture_text (line 1625) -> _tesseract_ocr_image (line 1474); src/pageindex_mcp/client.py::index() image-dominant OCR escalation (line 1097) -> _remote_pdf_to_markdown with force_full_page_ocr=True (line 1129); src/pageindex_mcp/converters.py::splice_figure_markers (line 1872) strips decorative markers -> empty flat_md
root_causes.suggested_fix: Two-pronged fix: (1) When Docling force-OCR still produces only `<!-- image -->` markers, fall back to standalone `tesseract_ocr_pdf_pages` (RFC-023 D7's rasterize-and-OCR pipeline already proven for CMap-crash recovery) to extract text directly from rasterized pages, bypassing Docling's PictureItem classification entirely. (2) In `_recover_picture_text`, when a full-page-coverage-exempted region yields OCR text from Tesseract, ensure that text is treated as prose content (not image-block OCR) -- the text should be spliced into the markdown body as a prose block, not hidden behind an `<!-- image -->` marker that gets stripped. The `_document_level_text_fallback` function (converters.py line 1559) partially addresses this for thin markdown, but its char threshold and heading-ratio gate may not fire for documents that are ENTIRELY image markers.

root_causes.root_cause: validate_tree exits early on node_count<3/depth<2 (lines 1053-1056) BEFORE the garble check (line 1057), so numeric-junk text that produces a minimal tree gets reason 'node_count<3' instead of 'garbling'. OCR escalation (client.py line 965) only fires for reason in ('garbling','node_garbling'), so recovery never triggers. The doc enters the flat path where _flat_text_is_garbled (helpers.py line 2069) operates on raw markdown INCLUDING formatting characters (headers, pipes, whitespace) that dilute heuristic ratios (e.g. digit ratio drops below the 60% threshold in _is_garbled_blob line 884). The doc is persisted with garbled content. classify_verdict then correctly detects garbling(ratio=1.00) via _tree_is_garbled on the BLOCK-TEXT-ONLY synthetic structure (where formatting is stripped), but this is scoring-only -- there is no recovery hook from classify_verdict's garble detection. The garbling is detected too late to trigger OCR recovery.
root_causes.code_path: client.py:index() -> validate_tree() exits at helpers.py:1053 (node_count<3) -> client.py:1175 flat_doc_routing -> _flat_text_is_garbled(raw_markdown) at helpers.py:2086 returns False (digit ratio diluted by markdown formatting) -> route_and_extract_flat -> classify_verdict(synthetic_structure) at helpers.py:1211 -> _tree_is_garbled returns True on block text -> returns MARGINAL garbling(ratio=1.00) -> save_flat_doc persists garbled content
root_causes.suggested_fix: Two-part fix: (1) In _flat_text_is_garbled (helpers.py:2069), strip markdown formatting (headers, pipes, whitespace, HTML comments) before calling _is_garbled_blob, matching what classify_verdict sees via _flatten_tree_text on the synthetic structure. (2) Add a post-classify_verdict gate in client.py's flat path (after line 1340): if classify_verdict returns effectively_garbled with garble_ratio >= a threshold (e.g. 0.50), escalate to OCR before save_flat_doc rather than persisting garbled content as MARGINAL. This closes both the _flat_text_is_garbled detection gap AND adds a safety net at classify_verdict.

root_causes.root_cause: CMap Latin-gibberish garbling (character substitutions from broken font encodings producing valid-looking Latin characters) is completely invisible to _is_garbled_blob when expected_script is 'Latn'. The Latin-gibberish check (helpers.py line 907) only fires when expected_script != 'Latn'. For German documents, expected_script='Latn', so CMap mojibake that substitutes e.g. umlauts/ligatures with random Latin characters passes ALL heuristics: no null bytes, no PUA, no excess digits, no control chars, no token repetition. Both validate_tree (line 1057, with expected_script='Latn') and classify_verdict (line 1211, with no expected_script) miss the garbling entirely. The per-node garble check (_garble_check_nodes at line 1067) also misses it because _is_garbled_blob returns False per-node for the same reason. With garbling undetected, effectively_garbled=False, and the RFC-024 PASS_MAX_LEAF_RATIO threshold increase from 0.20 to 0.30 further relaxed the PASS gate, resulting in PASS with empty verdict_reason despite 81/132 nodes being garbled content.
root_causes.code_path: client.py:index() -> validate_tree(expected_script='Latn') at helpers.py:1057 -> _tree_is_garbled(expected_script='Latn') returns False -> validate_tree passes -> save_doc persists garbled tree -> classify_verdict at helpers.py:1211 -> _tree_is_garbled(no expected_script) returns False -> garbled=False, effectively_garbled=False -> PASS gate (line 1235): node_count=132>=3, depth>=2, max_leaf_ratio<0.30, not effectively_garbled -> returns ('PASS', '')
root_causes.suggested_fix: Add a Latin-on-Latin garble detection heuristic in _is_garbled_blob. Options: (1) Character bigram/trigram frequency analysis against known language models (German, English) to detect whether text forms plausible words; (2) Dictionary coverage check -- if fewer than N% of whitespace-separated tokens appear in a language dictionary, flag as garbled; (3) Vowel-consonant ratio check -- CMap mojibake often produces consonant-heavy nonsense. The heuristic should be gated behind a minimum text length (>500 chars) and a configurable env var toggle to avoid false positives on technical/specialized documents.

root_causes.root_cause: The _document_level_text_fallback function in converters.py uses a fixed absolute threshold (_DOC_TEXT_FALLBACK_MIN_CHARS=100) that does not scale with document page count or expected content volume. For the uae_numbers landscape PDF, Docling's TableFormer fragments dense numeric tables into 748 chars of sparse text across 76 blocks — well above the 100-char floor, so the pdfium whole-document fallback never fires. The RFC-025 D1 secondary trigger (chars-per-heading < 50) also does not help because table-only documents have zero headings (heading_count=0, so chars/max(0,1) = 748 > 50). No other recovery path (OCR, clip_text, picture splice) successfully recovers the table content. This stall has persisted across Runs 7, 8, and 9 with identical 748/764 char counts. RFC-025 explicitly acknowledged this as 'Numeric table fragmentation; not garble-related' but deferred a fix.
root_causes.code_path: src/pageindex_mcp/converters.py::_document_level_text_fallback (lines 1559-1622), specifically the threshold check at lines 1576-1581
root_causes.suggested_fix: Add a page-count-aware threshold to _document_level_text_fallback: when total_chars / page_count falls below a per-page floor (e.g., 500 chars/page for a typical document), fire the pdfium fallback regardless of the absolute threshold. This requires passing pdf_path's page count into the function (pypdfium2 is already imported in the try block). Additionally, consider adding a Docling TableFormer quality check that detects fragmented numeric tables (many blocks with very few chars each) and fires a targeted table-extraction fallback.

root_causes.root_cause: Federal Decree-Law No. (47) of 2021 dropped from depth-2 (Run 8, tree path) to depth-1 (Run 9, flat path), causing a tree-to-flat routing switch. The validate_tree gate (helpers.py line 1055-1056) rejects depth<2 with reason 'depth<2', which routes the document to the flat path. The flat-path char counting via _flat_block_text (helpers.py line 2233) produces 13.4k chars vs the tree-path _flatten_tree_text (helpers.py line 554) which counted 24.3k chars in Run 8. The ~45% char reduction is at least partially a measurement difference from the path switch, not pure content loss. The depth drop itself likely stems from Docling non-determinism in heading-level inference (a known issue documented in RFC-025 D0), since no RFC-025 code change modifies heading-depth inference functions (_recover_heading_depth, _patch_hierarchical_infer, _repromote_numbered_headings). The verdict improved (MARGINAL->PASS) because the flat path's cat_b_promoted promotion gate (helpers.py line 1250-1266) is more lenient than the tree PASS gate's depth>=2 requirement.
root_causes.code_path: src/pageindex_mcp/helpers.py::validate_tree (line 1055-1056 depth<2 gate) -> src/pageindex_mcp/client.py flat routing (line 1175) -> src/pageindex_mcp/helpers.py::classify_verdict cat_b_promoted (line 1250-1266)
root_causes.suggested_fix: Two-part fix: (1) Add a depth-stability hysteresis similar to RFC-025 D0's max_leaf_ratio hysteresis: when prior_verdict was PASS or MARGINAL with a tree structure and depth was >= 2, allow depth=1 trees to remain on the tree path (depth hysteresis band). (2) Investigate whether the flat-path char count should include equivalent content to the tree-path count (title text, etc.) so that routing-path switches do not create phantom char regressions in audit metrics.

needs_doc_drilldown.reason: The depth drop from 2 to 1 between Run 8 and Run 9 could be Docling non-determinism (known issue per RFC-025 D0) or could be caused by RFC-025 D1's region-aware text check indirectly affecting Docling's heading detection through changed picture-region handling. root_causes.suggested_fix: Two-pronged fix: (1) When Docling force-OCR still produces only `<!-- image -->` markers, fall back to standalone `tesseract_ocr_pdf_pages` (RFC-023 D7's rasterize-and-OCR pipeline already proven for CMap-crash recovery) to extract text directly from rasterized pages, bypassing Docling's PictureItem classification entirely. (2) In `_recover_picture_text`, when a full-page-coverage-exempted region yields OCR text from Tesseract, ensure that text is treated as prose content (not image-block OCR) -- the text should be spliced into the markdown body as a prose block, not hidden behind an `<!-- image -->` marker that gets stripped. root_causes.root_cause: validate_tree exits early on node_count<3/depth<2 (lines 1053-1056) BEFORE the garble check (line 1057), so numeric-junk text that produces a minimal tree gets reason 'node_count<3' instead of 'garbling'. OCR escalation (client.py line 965) only fires for reason in ('garbling','node_garbling'), so recovery never triggers. The doc enters the flat path where _flat_text_is_garbled (helpers.py line 2069) operates on raw markdown INCLUDING formatting characters (headers, pipes, whitespace) that dilute heuristic ratios (e.g. digit ratio drops below the 60% threshold in _is_garbled_blob line 884). The doc is persisted with garbled content. classify_verdict then correctly detects garbling(ratio=1.00) via _tree_is_garbled on the BLOCK-TEXT-ONLY synthetic structure (where formatting is stripped), but this is scoring-only -- there is no recovery hook from classify_verdict's garble detection. The garbling is detected too late to trigger OCR recovery.

(2) Add a post-classify_verdict gate in client.py's flat path (after line 1340): if classify_verdict returns effectively_garbled with garble_ratio >= a threshold (e.g. 0.50), escalate to OCR before save_flat_doc rather than persisting garbled content as MARGINAL. This closes both the _flat_text_is_garbled detection gap AND adds a safety net at classify_verdict.

root_causes.root_cause: CMap Latin-gibberish garbling (character substitutions from broken font encodings producing valid-looking Latin characters) is completely invisible to _is_garbled_blob when expected_script is 'Latn'. The Latin-gibberish check (helpers.py line 907) only fires when expected_script != 'Latn'. For German documents, expected_script='Latn', so CMap mojibake that substitutes e.g. umlauts/ligatures with random Latin characters passes ALL heuristics: no null bytes, no PUA, no excess digits, no control chars, no token repetition. Both validate_tree (line 1057, with expected_script='Latn') and classify_verdict (line 1211, with no expected_script) miss the garbling entirely. The per-node garble check (_garble_check_nodes at line 1067) also misses it because _is_garbled_blob returns False per-node for the same reason. With garbling undetected, effectively_garbled=False, and the RFC-024 PASS_MAX_LEAF_RATIO threshold increase from 0.20 to 0.30 further relaxed the PASS gate, resulting in PASS with empty verdict_reason despite 81/132 nodes being garbled content.
root_causes.code_path: client.py:index() -> validate_tree(expected_script='Latn') at helpers.py:1057 -> _tree_is_garbled(expected_script='Latn') returns False -> validate_tree passes -> save_doc persists garbled tree -> classify_verdict at helpers.py:1211 -> _tree_is_garbled(no expected_script) returns False -> garbled=False, effectively_garbled=False -> PASS gate (line 1235): node_count=132>=3, depth>=2, max_leaf_ratio<0.30, not effectively_garbled -> returns ('PASS', '')
root_causes.suggested_fix: Add a Latin-on-Latin garble detection heuristic in _is_garbled_blob. Options: (1) Character bigram/trigram frequency analysis against known language models (German, English) to detect whether text forms plausible words; (2) Dictionary coverage check -- if fewer than N% of whitespace-separated tokens appear in a language dictionary, flag as garbled; (3) Vowel-consonant ratio check -- CMap mojibake often produces consonant-heavy nonsense. The heuristic should be gated behind a minimum text length (>500 chars) and a configurable env var toggle to avoid false positives on technical/specialized documents.

root_causes.root_cause: The _document_level_text_fallback function in converters.py uses a fixed absolute threshold (_DOC_TEXT_FALLBACK_MIN_CHARS=100) that does not scale with document page count or expected content volume. For the uae_numbers landscape PDF, Docling's TableFormer fragments dense numeric tables into 748 chars of sparse text across 76 blocks — well above the 100-char floor, so the pdfium whole-document fallback never fires. The RFC-025 D1 secondary trigger (chars-per-heading < 50) also does not help because table-only documents have zero headings (heading_count=0, so chars/max(0,1) = 748 > 50). No other recovery path (OCR, clip_text, picture splice) successfully recovers the table content. This stall has persisted across Runs 7, 8, and 9 with identical 748/764 char counts. RFC-025 explicitly acknowledged this as 'Numeric table fragmentation; not garble-related' but deferred a fix.
root_causes.code_path: src/pageindex_mcp/converters.py::_document_level_text_fallback (lines 1559-1622), specifically the threshold check at lines 1576-1581
root_causes.suggested_fix: Add a page-count-aware threshold to _document_level_text_fallback: when total_chars / page_count falls below a per-page floor (e.g., 500 chars/page for a typical document), fire the pdfium fallback regardless of the absolute threshold. This requires passing pdf_path's page count into the function (pypdfium2 is already imported in the try block). Additionally, consider adding a Docling TableFormer quality check that detects fragmented numeric tables (many blocks with very few chars each) and fires a targeted table-extraction fallback.

root_causes.root_cause: Federal Decree-Law No. (47) of 2021 dropped from depth-2 (Run 8, tree path) to depth-1 (Run 9, flat path), causing a tree-to-flat routing switch. The validate_tree gate (helpers.py line 1055-1056) rejects depth<2 with reason 'depth<2', which routes the document to the flat path. The flat-path char counting via _flat_block_text (helpers.py line 2233) produces 13.4k chars vs the tree-path _flatten_tree_text (helpers.py line 554) which counted 24.3k chars in Run 8. The ~45% char reduction is at least partially a measurement difference from the path switch, not pure content loss. The depth drop itself likely stems from Docling non-determinism in heading-level inference (a known issue documented in RFC-025 D0), since no RFC-025 code change modifies heading-depth inference functions (_recover_heading_depth, _patch_hierarchical_infer, _repromote_numbered_headings). The verdict improved (MARGINAL->PASS) because the flat path's cat_b_promoted promotion gate (helpers.py line 1250-1266) is more lenient than the tree PASS gate's depth>=2 requirement.

root_causes.suggested_fix: Two-part fix: (1) Add a depth-stability hysteresis similar to RFC-025 D0's max_leaf_ratio hysteresis: when prior_verdict was PASS or MARGINAL with a tree structure and depth was >= 2, allow depth=1 trees to remain on the tree path (depth hysteresis band). (2) Investigate whether the flat-path char count should include equivalent content to the tree-path count (title text, etc.) so that routing-path switches do not create phantom char regressions in audit metrics.
